info.title: NSchema
info.description: A declarative database schema migration tool built for .NET

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: A declarative database schema migration tool.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help and usage information

options.name: --version
options.description: Show version information

options.name: --no-color
options.description: Disable colored output. [default: False]

options.name: --directory
options.description: Project directory to run in. Defaults to the current directory.

options.name: --environment
options.description: Target environment. Layers the matching *.env.<name>.sql overlay files over the base project.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit machine-readable NDJSON output instead of formatted text (shorthand for --format json). [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Output format: text (default), json, or markdown (for a PR comment or CI job summary).

options.name: --no-init
options.description: Don't restore plugins; use only what's already cached, failing if a pinned plugin is missing. [default: False]

options.name: --verbose
options.description: Show verbose diagnostic detail (files read, object counts, per-run internals). [default: False]

options.name: --quiet
options.description: Suppress progress narration; show only outcomes, warnings, and results. [default: False]

commands.name: init
commands.description: Restore the provider and backend plugins pinned in the project configuration, locking declared ranges.

commands.name: new
commands.description: Create a new project in the current directory.

options.name: --force
options.description: Scaffold even in a non-empty directory, overwriting any files. [default: False]

options.name: --database
options.description: Database provider to scaffold configuration for: postgres (default), sqlite, or sqlserver.

options.name: --state
options.description: State backend to scaffold configuration for: file (default) or s3.

options.name: --set
options.description: Answer a plugin's scaffolding question up front, as key=value. Repeatable; skips the prompt.

options.name: --no-init
options.description: Skip resolving and locking the scaffolded plugins; run 'nschema init' yourself later. [default: False]

commands.name: validate
commands.description: Validate the desired schema without contacting a database or state store.

commands.name: format
commands.description: Reformat .sql DDL files to a canonical layout (in place, or check with --check).

options.name: --check
options.description: Don't write changes; list the files that need formatting and exit 2 if any do. [default: False]

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: A .sql file or a directory to format (recursively), or '-' to read stdin and write stdout. Defaults to the current directory. [default: .]

commands.name: plan
commands.description: Compute and show the migration plan without applying it. Use --destroy to preview a teardown instead.

options.name: --scope
options.description: Limit the plan to a schema ('app') or an object ('app.orders'). May be specified multiple times.

options.name: --destructive-actions
options.description: Policy when the plan contains destructive actions: Error (default), Warn, Allow, or Ignore.

options.name: --data-hazards
options.description: Policy when the plan contains changes that can fail on existing data: Error, Warn (default), Allow, or Ignore.

options.name: --destroy
options.description: Preview the plan that "destroy" would run to tear the managed schema down, without applying it. [default: False]

options.name: --out
options.description: Write the computed plan to this file so it can be replayed later with apply --plan-file.

options.name: --detailed-exitcode
options.description: Return a detailed exit code: 0 = no changes, 2 = changes present (errors remain 1). For CI gating. [default: False]

options.name: --ephemeral
options.description: Run against an in-memory state store discarded when the command exits, instead of a configured STATE store — for CI runs against disposable databases. Run-once script history does not persist. [default: False]

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show a saved plan file's diff and SQL.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: The saved plan file (from `plan --out`) to show. Renders its diff and SQL without contacting the database or state store.

commands.name: apply
commands.description: Compute the plan and apply it to the target database.

options.name: --scope
options.description: Limit the migration to a schema ('app') or an object ('app.orders'). May be specified multiple times.

options.name: --destructive-actions
options.description: Policy when the plan contains destructive actions: Error (default), Warn, Allow, or Ignore.

options.name: --data-hazards
options.description: Policy when the plan contains changes that can fail on existing data: Error, Warn (default), Allow, or Ignore.

options.name: --auto-approve
options.description: Skip the interactive confirmation prompt and apply the plan immediately. [default: False]

options.name: --plan-file
options.description: Apply a plan previously saved with plan --out.

options.name: --no-lock
options.description: Apply without acquiring the state lock. [default: False]

options.name: --no-refresh
options.description: Plan against the recorded state as-is, without capturing the live schema first. [default: False]

options.name: --ephemeral
options.description: Run against an in-memory state store instead of a configured STATE store. [default: False]

commands.name: refresh
commands.description: Read the live schema and write it to the state store.

options.name: --no-lock
options.description: Refresh without acquiring the state lock. You take responsibility for preventing concurrent runs (e.g. when operating under a manually-held lock). [default: False]

options.name: --force
options.description: Replace an existing state payload that cannot be read, resetting the script ledger. Without it, an unreadable payload fails the refresh. [default: False]

commands.name: import
commands.description: Read the live database schema and write it as desired-schema source files.

options.name: --scope
options.description: Limit the import to a schema ('app') or an object ('app.orders'). May be specified multiple times.

options.name: --out-dir
options.description: Directory to write the imported SQL files into. Defaults to the current directory.

options.name: --force
options.description: Overwrite existing .sql files in the output directory. [default: False]

commands.name: destroy
commands.description: Drop all managed schema objects from the target database.

options.name: --auto-approve
options.description: Skip the interactive confirmation prompt and tear down the schema immediately. [default: False]

options.name: --no-lock
options.description: Tear down without acquiring the state lock. [default: False]

options.name: --no-refresh
options.description: Plan the teardown against the recorded state as-is, without capturing the live schema first. [default: False]

options.name: --ephemeral
options.description: Run against an in-memory state store, instead of a configured STATE store. [default: False]

commands.name: state
commands.description: Inspect and manage the recorded schema state.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show the recorded schema state — from the configured store, or a state file given directly.

options.name: --scope
options.description: Limit the output to a schema ('app') or an object ('app.orders'). May be specified multiple times.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: A state file to show directly, instead of the recorded state from the configured store. No backend configuration is required.

commands.name: pull
commands.description: Pull the raw recorded state payload from the configured store, for inspection, backup, or hand-editing before a push.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: Write the pulled state to this file instead of standard output.

commands.name: push
commands.description: Push a state payload to the configured store, replacing the recorded state. The payload is validated, then written byte-for-byte.

options.name: --no-lock
options.description: Push without acquiring the state lock. You take responsibility for preventing concurrent runs (e.g. when operating under a manually-held lock). [default: False]

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: The state payload to push, e.g. a pulled state file after hand-editing.

commands.name: script
commands.description: Manage the script executions recorded in the state.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the script executions recorded in the state.

commands.name: hash
commands.description: Compute the body hash of the project's scripts.

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The declared name of a script. Omit to list every declaration with its hash.

commands.name: taint
commands.description: Remove a script's recorded execution from the state, so it runs again on the next apply.

options.name: --no-lock
options.description: Taint without acquiring the state lock. You take responsibility for preventing concurrent runs (e.g. when operating under a manually-held lock). [default: False]

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The declared name of the script whose recorded execution should be removed.

commands.name: untaint
commands.description: Record a script as executed without running it, so later plans skip it — e.g. after rebuilding lost state with refresh.

options.name: --no-lock
options.description: Untaint without acquiring the state lock. You take responsibility for preventing concurrent runs (e.g. when operating under a manually-held lock). [default: False]

arguments.name: NAME
arguments.description: The declared name of the script to record as executed.

commands.name: database
commands.description: Inspect the live database.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show the live database schema, read directly from the database via the provider.

options.name: --scope
options.description: Limit the output to a schema ('app') or an object ('app.orders'). May be specified multiple times.

commands.name: drift
commands.description: Check whether the live database has drifted from the recorded state.

options.name: --scope
options.description: Limit the drift check to a schema ('app') or an object ('app.orders'). May be specified multiple times.

options.name: --detailed-exitcode
options.description: Return a detailed exit code: 0 = no drift, 2 = drift detected (errors remain 1). For CI gating. [default: False]

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Check that the configured database and state store are reachable and healthy.

commands.name: lock
commands.description: Inspect and manage the state lock.

commands.name: status
commands.description: Show whether the state store is currently locked, and by whom.

options.name: --detailed-exitcode
options.description: Return a detailed exit code: 0 = not locked, 2 = locked (errors remain 1). For CI gating. [default: False]

commands.name: acquire
commands.description: Take the state lock and hold it, e.g. while running out-of-band checks before a migration.

options.name: --reason
options.description: A note recorded on the lock describing why it's held, shown by 'lock status' (default: manual).

options.name: --ttl
options.description: Optional lifetime after which the lock is reported as expired (e.g. 30m, 2h, 90s, 1d). The lock is never auto-released.

commands.name: release
commands.description: Release the state lock, even if an operation still holds it.

options.name: --auto-approve
options.description: Skip the interactive confirmation prompt and release the lock immediately. [default: False]

options.name: --force
options.description: Release whatever lock is held without naming its id. Use when you can't read the id first; otherwise pass the lock id so a lock taken since isn't released by mistake. [default: False]

arguments.name: LOCK_ID
arguments.description: The id of the lock to release, taken from the error of the blocked operation or from lock status. The release is refused if it no longer matches the held lock (a safety check). Required unless --force is given to release whatever lock is held.

commands.name: plugin
commands.description: Inspect the project's provider and backend plugins, and manage the plugin cache.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the provider and backend plugins this project uses, and whether each is restored.

commands.name: show
commands.description: Show the detail of one of the project's plugins, including its cache status.

arguments.name: LABEL
arguments.description: The label of the plugin to show, as declared by its PLUGIN statement (e.g. postgres, s3).

commands.name: update
commands.description: Re-resolve declared version ranges to their highest available version and rewrite the lockfile.

arguments.name: PLUGIN
arguments.description: The label of the plugin to update; omit to update every plugin declared with a range.

commands.name: outdated
commands.description: Show, for each project plugin, its pinned version against the newest its range allows and the newest available.

commands.name: cache
commands.description: Inspect and remove entries in the shared plugin cache (~/.nschema/plugins).

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the plugin packages restored in the shared cache, across all projects.

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Remove a plugin package from the shared cache, by package id and optional version.

arguments.name: PACKAGE
arguments.description: The plugin package id to remove from the cache (e.g. NSchema.Postgres).

arguments.name: VERSION
arguments.description: The specific version to remove. When omitted, every cached version of the package is removed.

commands.name: clear
commands.description: Remove every plugin from the shared cache. Each is re-restored on the next run (or 'nschema init').

commands.name: completion
commands.description: Output a shell tab-completion script for nschema, or install/uninstall it.

arguments.name: SHELL
arguments.description: The shell to target (bash, zsh, fish, pwsh).

commands.name: install
commands.description: Install the completion script into the shell's startup file.

arguments.name: SHELL
arguments.description: The shell to target (bash, zsh, fish, pwsh).

commands.name: uninstall
commands.description: Remove the completion script from the shell's startup file.

arguments.name: SHELL
arguments.description: The shell to target (bash, zsh, fish, pwsh).
